- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak or mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+2% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +1.5% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) in last 3–5 days, model underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.0% to avoid “sentiment lag” bias.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day horizon: if forecast is >+1.5% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 0.3–0.7% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment >0.15 for 3+ consecutive days, add 0.2–0.5% to forecast to reflect “sentiment lag correction”.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history: if last 3 days are volatile (±1.5%+), reduce forecast sensitivity to 1-day history; use 7-day weighted average for smoothing.
